name: search_overflow
description: Search session content moved out of context. Returns verbatim excerpts with file paths and line numbers.
first_use_guidance:
Guidance for reading later search_overflow answers in this turn:
- Only content moved out of context is searched (never canonical session history or project files), and every file the filters keep is scanned in full.
- Narrow with scope or file_pattern first; scope=all is a last resort.
- The footer reports files scanned plus matching line(s) that were selected but not written; those lines stay reachable by narrowing the query, scope, or file_pattern, or by raising max_results.
- Each matching line carries a reason marker; the legend is: >> whole-query phrase hit, >t typed-term hit, >b CJK-fragment hit (the phrase may be absent — verify with read_file), two spaces = context line.
- A zero-hit answer names what it scanned (files searched, file_pattern exclusions, unreadable files, and which terms came up empty; when nothing was scanned it says so and names the roots probed) and names the matching mode, so a case-insensitive zero hit rules out other casings too; read it as 'not found in this archive', not as proof the content never existed, and retry with a wider scope, more distinctive words, or case_sensitive=true to narrow to one specific casing.
- Excerpts window long lines around the match, with … marking elided text on either side, so a window is not the whole line: use read_file on the listed absolute path for the full line.

query.description: Search term (plain substring by default; is_regex=true for regex). A multi-word query matches lines holding any one of its words, and ranks lines holding the whole phrase highest, then lines holding all words close together, so a hit does not prove the phrase is present. For CJK queries the adjacent character pairs of each run of three or more characters match as well (at most 24 pairs per query, sampled across the whole query), so a hit may rest on a shared pair rather than the full run.

scope.description: Where to search (default: all). 'history' = overflow-history.md plus summary-sources/ (raw messages behind compressed summaries). 'tool_outputs' includes tool-overflow-compressed/, tool-overflow/, folded-tool-groups/, internal-note-overflow/, and context-checkpoints/. 'all' also includes history and preserved user/image context. Checkpoint bodies are unverified historical context.

file_pattern.description: Optional glob to restrict searched archive files, matched against the path relative to the archive root or the file name (e.g. '*execute_command*', '*internal-note-overflow*').

is_regex.description: Treat query as a regex (default: false, literal substring). The pattern is matched case-insensitively unless case_sensitive is true; an inline flag in the pattern itself (e.g. `(?i)`, `(?-i)`) overrides that.

case_sensitive.description: Case-sensitive match (default: false — matching ignores case by default, so the query also hits other casings; set true to narrow to one exact casing).

context_lines.description: Context lines around each match (default: 2, max: 5).

max_results.description: Max matching lines across all files (default: 50, max: 200). Raising it also raises the per-file ceiling, so one large file exposes more of its matching lines.
